## Academic Background

I hold a degree in Computer Engineering from the Universidade de Pernambuco (UPE, 2003–2008) and a Master's degree in Teleinformatics Engineering from the Universidade Federal do Ceará (UFC, 2011–2014), in the concentration area of Signals and Systems, followed by a postgraduate specialization in Information Systems Development and Management (Faculdade JK, 2014–2015). My master's thesis, advised by Prof. Dr. Guilherme de Alencar Barreto, developed prototype-based pattern classifiers optimized with differential evolution — an early exposure to computational intelligence, pattern recognition, and optimization that continues to inform how I approach quantitative problems, and that later led to a peer-reviewed conference paper. The full thesis and paper, with links, are listed on the [Publications](publications.qmd) page.

## Professional Trajectory

My professional path has been in information systems and data-intensive work in the Brazilian public sector for close to two decades, across roles at Policentro/Ecil, DATAPREV, the Ministry of Planning, and the Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU) — including experience with systems development, databases, data engineering and integration (ETL), business intelligence, workflow orchestration, and data mining. At the Ministry of Planning, I was part of the team behind the Brazilian Public Software program (Software Público Brasileiro), where I served as technical lead for an update of the program's Manual do Ofertante (Vendor's Manual) — see [Projects](projects.qmd). Since 2024, I have worked at the Institute for Applied Economic Research (Ipea), in the Coordenação de Sistemas de Informação (COSIS), within its data science and information technology area [TO BE VERIFIED: exact English title of my position; see the [CV](cv.qmd) page].

This experience is not the center of this website, but it is the foundation for the research direction described below: years spent turning institutional and public-sector problems into data and computational problems gave me both a strong computational base and direct, practical familiarity with the kind of systems and data that public-policy research draws on.

## Research Transition

Over the past several years, my interests have shifted from applied computational intelligence and public-sector data systems toward complex systems, network science, and agent-based modeling, with a growing focus on their application to computational economics and public policy. Concretely, this has included joining [LASPP](research.qmd#laspp), a research group at Ipea working on complex systems and their applications, completing a graduate course in complex systems at the University of São Paulo (USP) in 2025, and currently taking a course in agent-based economic models there as a special student. More detail on this trajectory and the questions motivating it is on the [Research](research.qmd) page.

## Current Interests

My current interests are described in more detail on the [Research](research.qmd) page: complex systems and network science, agent-based modeling, computational economics, and computational approaches to public policy.

This website does not currently represent an active PhD application announcement — this line will be updated if and when that changes.

## Beyond Research

Outside of research, I spend time with family, enjoy sports, reading, and following developments in science more broadly, and like getting outdoors when I can.
